page_builder.heading: Gardens that belong where they are
page_builder.subheading: Northfold is a landscape and garden design studio in Northumberland. We design gardens across the north of England that suit the place, the people and the weather.

content.text: We design private gardens, small public spaces and the occasional orchard. Every one starts with the same question: what does this place want to be, and what do the people who use it need from it?
The answer is rarely the same twice. But it nearly always involves good soil, the right plants in the right place, and a design simple enough to still make sense in twenty years.

page_builder.caption: A planting plan in progress at the studio.

page_builder.quote: They listened properly, and the garden they drew was better than the one we'd imagined.

page_builder.heading: Thinking about your garden?
page_builder.text: Tell us a little about it, and we'll arrange a first visit.

page_builder.heading: How we can help
page_builder.subheading: From a single planting plan to a full design and build, we can be as involved as you'd like.

content.text: Garden design
A full design for your garden: a survey, a concept, a detailed layout and construction drawings, and a planting plan. We'll help you find a contractor, or work with one you already know.
Planting plans
If the layout is sorted and you just need the planting, we'll draw a detailed plan with a plant schedule, quantities and suppliers. We can set the plants out on the day, too.
Consultations
A two-hour visit, with a walk round, plenty of questions and a written summary afterwards. Useful if you're not sure where to start, or just want a second opinion.

page_builder.caption: Stone, timber and gravel samples for a terrace in Durham.

page_builder.quote: The consultation alone saved us from at least two very expensive mistakes.

content.text: Aftercare
For the first two years, a garden is still settling in. We offer seasonal visits to check on planting, adjust anything that isn't working, and guide whoever looks after it day to day.

page_builder.text:
## Look first

Every project starts with time on site: digging holes, watching where the sun goes, noticing what grows well next door. The soil and the weather decide more about a garden than any drawing.

## Keep it simple

Good gardens tend to have fewer ideas, done well. We'd rather repeat a handful of plants that thrive than squeeze in fifty that struggle.

page_builder.caption: A meadow strip, mown through with a path, in its third summer.

page_builder.quote: The best compliment we get is when someone asks who designed the garden, and the answer is nobody they'd have noticed.

page_builder.text:
## Build for the long run

We choose materials that age well and plants that live a long time. A garden should get better every year for decades, not look its best on day one and decline from there.

## Leave room for nature

Seedheads left standing, a strip of long grass, a pond with a shallow edge. Small things add up, and they rarely cost more.

## What it's like here

We work from an old dairy on a farm outside Hexham, with a trial garden, a long table and a lot of tea. Most of us spend two or three days a week on site and the rest in the studio.

We're a small team, so everyone gets involved in the whole of a project, from the first visit to the last plant.

page_builder.caption: Friday lunch in the trial garden.

page_builder.quote: I've learned more in a year here than in the five before it, and I've never once dreaded a Monday.

page_builder.text:
## Current roles

### Junior garden designer

Full time, based at the studio. You'll have a qualification in garden or landscape design, or be close to one, and a real interest in plants. You'll work alongside our senior designers on surveys, drawings and planting plans.

### What we offer

- A fair salary, reviewed every year
- Twenty-eight days' holiday, plus the week between Christmas and New Year
- Training and garden visits, paid for by the studio

content.text: We design private gardens, small public spaces and the occasional orchard. Every one starts with the same question: what does this place want to be, and what do the people who use it need from it?
The answer is rarely the same twice. But it nearly always involves good soil, the right plants in the right place, and a design simple enough to still make sense in twenty years.

page_builder.caption: A planting plan in progress at the studio.

page_builder.quote: They listened properly, and the garden they drew was better than the one we'd imagined.

page_builder.heading: Thinking about your garden?
page_builder.text: Tell us a little about it, and we'll arrange a first visit.

page_builder.heading: How we can help
page_builder.subheading: From a single planting plan to a full design and build, we can be as involved as you'd like.

page_builder.text:
## Garden design

A full design for your garden: a survey, a concept, a detailed layout and construction drawings, and a planting plan. We'll help you find a contractor, or work with one you already know.

## Planting plans

If the layout is sorted and you just need the planting, we'll draw a detailed plan with a plant schedule, quantities and suppliers. We can set the plants out on the day, too.

## Consultations

A two-hour visit, with a walk round, plenty of questions and a written summary afterwards. Useful if you're not sure where to start, or just want a second opinion.

page_builder.caption: Stone, timber and gravel samples for a terrace in Durham.

page_builder.quote: The consultation alone saved us from at least two very expensive mistakes.

page_builder.text:
## Aftercare

For the first two years, a garden is still settling in. We offer seasonal visits to check on planting, adjust anything that isn't working, and guide whoever looks after it day to day.

page_builder.subheading: Northfold was started in 2014 by two garden designers who wanted to spend less time in meetings and more time outside.

page_builder.text:
## Who we are

We're a team of five: three designers, a project manager and a horticulturist who keeps the rest of us honest. We work from an old dairy outside Hexham, with a trial garden out the back where we test plants before they go into anyone else's garden.

We've designed more than two hundred gardens across Northumberland, Durham, Cumbria and Yorkshire, from back yards in Newcastle to walled gardens and country estates.

page_builder.caption: The studio at Low Fold Farm.

page_builder.quote: A garden should look as though it has always been there, even on the day it's finished.

page_builder.text:
## What we care about

- Plants that suit the soil and the climate, so they thrive without fuss
- Materials that weather well and come from nearby where we can manage it
- Gardens that work for wildlife as well as for people
- Being straight with clients about cost, time and what a garden will need from them

page_builder.heading: Want to work with us?
page_builder.text: We take on around twenty new gardens a year. Get in touch early if you have a season in mind.

page_builder.heading: Start with the place
page_builder.subheading: We look hard at what's already there before we draw anything new.

page_builder.text:
## Look first

Every project starts with time on site: digging holes, watching where the sun goes, noticing what grows well next door. The soil and the weather decide more about a garden than any drawing.

## Keep it simple

Good gardens tend to have fewer ideas, done well. We'd rather repeat a handful of plants that thrive than squeeze in fifty that struggle.

page_builder.caption: A meadow strip, mown through with a path, in its third summer.

page_builder.quote: The best compliment we get is when someone asks who designed the garden, and the answer is nobody they'd have noticed.

page_builder.text:
## Build for the long run

We choose materials that age well and plants that live a long time. A garden should get better every year for decades, not look its best on day one and decline from there.

## Leave room for nature

Seedheads left standing, a strip of long grass, a pond with a shallow edge. Small things add up, and they rarely cost more.
